answer.label: Not Nikola Tesla — an unsourced modern quote
answer.sourceLine: This line is pinned on Tesla all over the internet, but it appears in none of his books, patents, lectures, letters, or interviews. Fact-checkers trace its earliest appearances only to around 2009–2010 — more than six decades after Tesla died — and conclude it is “not credibly attributed” to him. There is no documented primary source.

source.heading: Where it actually comes from

source.excerpt: If you only knew the magnificence of the 3, 6 and 9, then you would have the key to the universe.
trail: The line appears in none of Tesla’s writings; his Wikiquote entry does not list it in any section — not Sourced, not Disputed, not Misattributed.
A dedicated fact-check by TruthOrFiction concludes the quote “has not been credibly attributed to Nikola Tesla.”
The earliest instances fact-checkers could trace are a pseudoscience sales page and Flickr comments around 2009-2010 — over six decades after Tesla’s death in 1943.
source.excerptNote: No documented instance of Tesla writing or speaking these words has ever been produced.

author.name: Nikola Tesla
author.heading: About the man this is pinned on
author.bio: Nikola Tesla pioneered alternating-current power, the induction motor, and wireless-transmission experiments, becoming one of history’s most mythologized inventors. His reputation for eccentric habits and grand cosmic pronouncements makes him a magnet for invented “visionary” quotes. This numerological aphorism fits that legend — but it is a product of the internet era, not of anything Tesla is documented to have written or said.

misattribution.heading: Why this gets pinned on Tesla
misattribution.intro: The quote is one of the internet’s most-shared “Tesla” lines, but it has no home in his actual body of work.

items.why: The “magnificence of the 3, 6 and 9 … key to the universe” phrasing appears in no Tesla book, patent, lecture, letter, or interview. His Wikiquote entry does not list it at all.
Fact-checkers trace the line only to around 2009-2010 — a pseudoscience sales page and Flickr comments — decades after Tesla died in 1943.

misattribution.truthLine: The honest verdict: this is a modern, unsourced aphorism attached to Tesla’s name; per TruthOrFiction, it “has not been credibly attributed” to him.

context.heading: The real kernel
lead: Tesla genuinely had famous personal quirks — he favored actions in threes and was drawn to numbers divisible by three — and this reputation is what makes the “3, 6 and 9” quote feel plausible. But a documented fondness for the number three is not the same as a recorded statement that these digits are the “key to the universe.”
The specific line only entered circulation in the social-media era, where a poetic, mystical-sounding soundbite spreads faster than anyone stops to ask for a citation. No such citation exists.
context.pull: A documented fondness for a number is not a recorded sentence about the cosmos.
